subject: E-Commerce
title: Third-Party Sellers Take Over
description: A micro-lesson that makes Third-Party Sellers Take Over usable.

hook.text: Over 60% of products sold on Amazon come from third-party sellers, not Amazon itself. It's a marketplace now.

buildup.text: Amazon launched Marketplace in 2000. Anyone could list products alongside Amazon's own inventory.

discovery.text: Third-party sellers pay Amazon 15% of each sale plus fulfillment fees. Amazon earns without holding inventory.

twist.text: Amazon can see which third-party products sell best, then launch competing Amazon Basics versions for less.

climax.text: The marketplace model made Amazon less of a retailer and more of a platform that taxes all commerce.

punchline.text: 60% from third parties, 15% cut each. Amazon became the tax collector of.

quiz.question: What percentage of Amazon's sales come from third-party sellers?
